solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Free Latin book a Greek character returned

parts.note: liber is the Latin word for a book

indicators.note: returned means the Greek letter is sent back, read from right to left

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A schoolroom scene: a Latin textbook given away and a Greek letter handed back.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone is to set them at liberty, a straight verb synonym.

clue.text: Pulse member finally ate with hesitation

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
um is a sound of hesitation

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of ate

explanation.surface: A club member finally ate, hesitating over the pulses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' suggests a heartbeat; here it is a lentil or bean. 'with' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Peas, beans and lentils are pulses, edible seeds of the pea family.

clue.text: Inept type, one playing outside entrance to nightclub

indicators.note: outside means the player stands around the other letter

parts.note: a bugler is one who plays the bugle

indicators.note: entrance to takes the first letter of nightclub

explanation.surface: A clumsy musician playing outside a nightclub door.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who botches things through clumsiness is an incompetent sort.

clue.text: Like some religious leaders, babble endlessly in upset state?

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the word for babble is cut off

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chattering on at length

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the word in reads upwards

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: Clergy babbling endlessly in a state of upset.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'rabbit on' is British slang for to talk endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabbis are Jewish religious teachers, so this adjective describes such leaders.

clue.text: Dine at hotel abroad, eating most of hot baked food

indicators.note: eating means the shuffled letters take in the other piece
abroad suggests going astray, so the letters are rearranged
most of means the final letter of hot is dropped

explanation.surface: Dining at a foreign hotel, eating most of a hot baked dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' rearranges DINE AT HOTEL; 'eating' puts HO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Toad in the hole is a British dish of sausages baked in Yorkshire pudding batter.

clue.text: Popular retired doctor initially under such a cloud?

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, so the word for popular goes backwards

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letters of the words under and such

explanation.surface: A well-liked doctor has stepped down under a cloud of suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under a cloud' reads as disgrace, but the cloud is the definition and 'such' makes it a question of what kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A nimbus is a type of rain-bearing grey cloud, and also a halo, so it names a kind of cloud.

clue.text: Shrub identified by the Italian divorcee

parts.note: il is Italian for the
an ex is a former spouse

explanation.surface: An Italian divorcee is identified by a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Ilex is the holly genus, an evergreen bush.

clue.text: Graduate nurse in the past, one keeping judge's dog

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts
SEN was a State Enrolled Nurse, a former British grade
J is an abbreviation for judge
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A graduate who once nursed now keeps the judge's dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a barkless hunting hound from central Africa.

clue.text: Dance with girl born first

indicators.note: first means the girl and born come ahead of the word for with

parts.note: Sara is a girl's name
and means with or plus

explanation.surface: A dance with a girl born first.
explanation.definitionFit: The sarabande is a slow, stately Spanish dance in triple time.

clue.text: Mother's ruin? It's a trap

definitions.meaning: mother's ruin is an old British nickname for the spirit distilled with juniper

explanation.surface: A warning that a mother's downfall is a deliberate snare.
explanation.definitionFit: The spirit was nicknamed mother's ruin in Georgian London, and an animal snare is also called by the same short word.

clue.text: Problem supporter in east restrained by immobilising device

parts.note: a bra is an undergarment that supports

indicators.note: restrained by means held inside the other piece, so the compass letter sits within the device

parts.note: a Taser is a stun gun that immobilises its target
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A problem fan in the east is held back with a stun gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restrained by' puts E inside TASER to make TEASER.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle that taxes the mind is a problem, so the hyphenated phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Shaky persons, surely, skiing here?

indicators.note: shaky means unsteady, so the letters wobble into a new order

explanation.surface: Wobbly people are surely on the beginners' slopes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: shaky skiers belong on the gentle slopes.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentle beginners' runs at a ski resort are where novices learn.

clue.text: Amount of liquid woman, about 51, took regularly at first

indicators.note: about means going around, so the name wraps the other letters

parts.note: Millie is a woman's name
LI is 51 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letters of took and regularly

explanation.surface: A woman of about fifty-one drank regularly at first.
explanation.walkthrough: '51' reads as the woman's age, but it is a Roman numeral; 'took regularly' sounds like habitual drinking, yet only its initials count.
explanation.definitionFit: One thousandth of a litre is a small measured quantity of fluid.

clue.text: Shoemaker, one who behaves condescendingly

definitions.meaning: an old dialect word for a cobbler or shoemaker
someone who looks down on people of lower social standing

explanation.surface: A cobbler who acts superior to his customers.
explanation.definitionFit: The older sense is a cobbler; the modern sense is a person who looks down on those thought socially inferior.

clue.text: Mourner possibly, one putting up with oppressive atmosphere?

parts.note: a pall is a gloomy, oppressive atmosphere
a bearer is one who bears or tolerates

explanation.surface: A mourner perhaps, enduring a gloomy mood at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffin carriers at a funeral are often among the grieving.

clue.text: Bacon, for example, sent back in restaurants I traduced

indicators.note: sent back means the letters are read in reverse order, like a dish returned
in means the letters are found inside the run of words restaurants I traduced

explanation.surface: Bacon was sent back in restaurants that I slandered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' suggests breakfast sent back to the kitchen; it is Francis Bacon, the painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was a twentieth-century painter, so he is an example of a painter or creative.

clue.text: Joy Orwell originally found in European language

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the initial goes within the language

parts.note: Latin is a language

indicators.note: originally takes the first letter of Orwell

explanation.surface: Joy at an early Orwell manuscript turning up in a European language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts O inside LATIN, making LATION, which follows E.
explanation.definitionFit: Elation is great happiness and exhilaration, a synonym of delight.

clue.text: Shrub head of arboretum is able so to provide

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of arboretum

parts.note: can means is able to
thus means so, in this way

explanation.surface: The head of an arboretum is able to provide a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Acanthus is a Mediterranean plant with spiny leaves, often called bear's breech.

clue.text: Enclosure outside old abstainer's rural dwelling

indicators.note: outside means the enclosure goes round the other letters

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure
TT means teetotal, so a teetotaller is an abstainer

explanation.surface: A fence around an old teetotaller's country home.
explanation.definitionFit: A small house in the countryside is the classic country dwelling.

clue.text: Characteristic of monk to start to swim in northern river

indicators.note: in means the letter is put inside the northern river's letters

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: start to takes the opening letter of swim

explanation.surface: A monk's habit is to start swimming in a northern river.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaved crown is the traditional mark of a monk's head.

clue.text: Unknown East Ender's assistant, one emitting shrill cries

parts.note: Y is a mathematical unknown

indicators.note: an East Ender is a Cockney from London's East End, who drops the initial h

parts.note: a helper is an assistant

explanation.surface: An unknown Cockney's assistant who keeps squealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, from the East End of London, are stereotyped as dropping their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: To yelp is to give a sharp high cry, so someone or something that does so fits.

clue.text: Surround new visitor initially received by English club

indicators.note: received by means held inside the English club's letters

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of visitor

explanation.surface: New visitors are surrounded at an English club's reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Environ is a verb meaning to encircle, a synonym of surround.

clue.text: Heading for ball, supple and cheerful

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of ball

parts.note: lithe means supple

explanation.surface: Heading off to a ball, lithe and cheery.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means happy and carefree, a synonym of cheerful.

clue.text: Tyneside area containing popular square

definitions.note: nine is three squared, so it is a square number

indicators.note: containing means the area's letters hold the other piece

parts.note: NE is North East England, where Tyneside lies
in means popular

explanation.surface: A Tyneside district with a well-used town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' looks like a public place; it is a square number.
explanation.definitionFit: Three times three makes this number, so it is a perfect square in arithmetic.

clue.text: Extremely low in tree-trunk, harmful beetle

indicators.note: in means put inside the trunk, which wraps the edge letters

parts.note: a bole is the trunk of a tree

indicators.note: extremely takes the two end letters of low

parts.note: evil means harmful

explanation.surface: Low down in a tree trunk lives a destructive insect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harmful' looks like part of the definition but supplies EVIL; the definition is 'beetle'.
explanation.definitionFit: The boll weevil is a beetle that destroys cotton crops.

clue.text: Smile broadly, seeing supporting member

definitions.meaning: a horizontal timber or girder holding up a structure

explanation.surface: Smiling broadly at a member who supports you.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb is to grin radiantly; the noun is a load-bearing joist in a building.

clue.text: Domestic employee's husband taking ring across river

indicators.note: across means the husband and ring straddle the river, one on each side

parts.note: a keeper is a ring worn to guard a wedding ring
the Ouse is an English river

explanation.surface: A maid's husband takes a ring across the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employee's' is read as 'employee is'. 'taking' simply links H to KEEPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone paid to run a household is a domestic servant or staff member.

clue.text: Deserter? Not in the desert once!

definitions.meaning: a ... is someone who deserts, as ... leave a sinking ship
the Desert ... were the British 7th Armoured Division in North Africa; one not in the desert is no longer a Desert ...

explanation.surface: A deserter quips that once he was never in the desert.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat who abandons his side is called a rodent; the Desert Rats were a famous British army division.

clue.text: Raunchy crew in outskirts of Salisbury

indicators.note: in means the crew sits within the town's outer letters
outskirts of takes the first and last letters of Salisbury

parts.note: a crew is a team

explanation.surface: A racy film crew on the edge of Salisbury, a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy describes erotic or sexually charged scenes, a synonym of raunchy.

clue.text: Alienate new sergeant

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of sergeant are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new sergeant alienates his platoon.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to make someone hostile or distant, a synonym of alienate.
